text.p: Croatia recorded 21.5 million tourist overnights last year, or 67 percent more than in 1995, a daily reported on Wednesday.
Quoting data from the State Statistics Bureau, Slobodna Dalmacija said the number of foreign tourist overnights rose 94 percent to 16.6 million in 1996.

Germans, who were the most frequent visitors to Croatia's Adriatic coast before the former republic seceded from Yugoslavia in 1991, topped the list of foreign tourists in 1996, with 3.7 million overnights.
Slovenes, Czechs and Italians also made their come-back last year.
Before the 1991-95 war with its minority Serbs, Croatia lured thousands of tourists from home and abroad to its sunny islands and dented coast.
Croatian tourists accounted for 4.9 million overnight stays last year, up 12 percent from 1995.
Most tourists visited the Istrian peninsula in the northern Adriatic, which recorded 9.5 million overnights.
